articles.title: Anthropic Releases Claude 4 Opus with Expanded 2M Token Context Window
articles.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude 4 Opus, featuring a breakthrough 2 million token context window that allows processing of entire codebases and lengthy document collections in a single pass. The model demonstrates significant improvements in multi-step reasoning and shows reduced hallucination rates compared to its predecessor. Early benchmarks from independent researchers suggest it surpasses competing frontier models on several long-context retrieval tasks.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Agent Framework Now Available to Enterprise Customers
articles.summary: Google DeepMind has opened its Gemini Agent Framework to enterprise customers, enabling businesses to deploy autonomous multi-agent systems capable of handling complex, long-horizon workflows. The framework includes built-in safety guardrails and audit logs designed to satisfy regulatory requirements in finance and healthcare sectors. Several Fortune 500 companies have already piloted the system, reporting up to 40% reduction in operational overhead for repetitive knowledge work.

articles.title: OpenAI Publishes New Safety Framework for Autonomous AI Systems
articles.summary: OpenAI released a detailed technical whitepaper outlining its updated safety protocols for agentic and autonomous AI deployments, including a tiered permission model and mandatory human-in-the-loop checkpoints for high-stakes decisions. The framework responds to growing regulatory pressure in the EU and US, where lawmakers have demanded clearer accountability structures for AI agents operating in critical infrastructure. Critics from the AI safety community praised portions of the document while calling for stronger third-party audit requirements.

articles.title: Meta Unveils Multimodal Llama 4 Scout with Real-Time Video Understanding
articles.summary: Meta has announced Llama 4 Scout, an open-weight multimodal model capable of processing real-time video streams alongside text and audio inputs simultaneously. The model is optimized to run on consumer-grade hardware and is being released under Meta's open license, continuing the company's strategy of competing through openness. Researchers are already exploring applications in robotics, live sports analytics, and accessibility tools for the visually impaired.

articles.title: Microsoft Integrates RAG-Powered Copilot Directly Into Windows 12 OS Layer
articles.summary: Microsoft has begun rolling out a deep OS-level integration of its Copilot assistant in Windows 12, leveraging retrieval-augmented generation to index and search users' local files, emails, and browser history in real time. The feature, called Copilot Recall Pro, builds on the controversial Recall feature but adds opt-in granular privacy controls following last year's backlash. Enterprise administrators can set retention and indexing policies through Group Policy, addressing earlier security concerns raised by IT departments.

articles.title: Stanford HAI Report Warns of Accelerating AI Concentration Among Five Firms
articles.summary: Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute released its 2026 mid-year AI Index, highlighting that over 78% of frontier model compute is now controlled by just five technology companies, raising antitrust and geopolitical concerns. The report also notes that AI-related patent filings have grown 62% year-over-year, while academic institutions struggle to access sufficient compute for independent safety research. Policy recommendations include a proposed international compute registry and expanded government grants for non-commercial AI research.

articles.title: Mistral Launches Le Chat Pro with Integrated Code Interpreter and Web Search
articles.summary: French AI startup Mistral has upgraded its Le Chat assistant to a Pro tier, adding a sandboxed code interpreter, real-time web search, and file analysis tools aimed squarely at competing with ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro. The new offering is priced aggressively at €14 per month and includes API access, making it attractive for European businesses seeking GDPR-compliant alternatives to US-based providers. The release coincides with renewed EU investment in sovereign AI infrastructure under the AI Sovereignty Act passed earlier this year.

articles.title: UC Berkeley Researchers Demonstrate LLM Self-Correction via Iterative Critique Loops
articles.summary: A team at UC Berkeley has published a paper showing that large language models can achieve near-human-level error correction on complex mathematical proofs by running iterative self-critique loops without external feedback. The technique, dubbed Recursive Reflective Refinement (R3), reduces errors by up to 34% compared to standard chain-of-thought prompting on competition-level math benchmarks. The authors argue the approach could be adapted to improve reliability in scientific reasoning and legal document analysis.
